gaps.sentence: We had a ___ of fun at the fair.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of fun' is the fixed phrase; 'fun' is uncountable and the article 'a' forces 'lot'.

gaps.sentence: ___ of work has been done on the house since we bought it.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of work' fits the pattern '___ of work'; 'much of work' would need 'the', and 'few' is for countables.
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so 'how much' is used.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: The twins are ___ over six feet tall.
gaps.explanation: 'Both' is used for exactly two; 'all' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: ___ the students passed with good grades.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the + noun' use 'most of': 'Most of the students'; 'most the students' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: We inspected the four bridges, but ___ of them was safe.
gaps.explanation: 'None of them was ...' is used for three or more items; 'neither' is only for two.

gaps.hint: price per item comes at the end
gaps.explanation: 'Fifteen pounds each' means fifteen pounds per ticket; 'every' cannot stand alone in this position.
